summary: Session lock collision from edge health probe causes mixed-variant responses during canary promote
description:
Issue summary:
Customer observed intermittent mixed model outputs after we started a weighted canary promote of llama-3b-v2-canary. Some sessions that had been pinned to the stable model returned responses from the canary variant or returned 502s mid-stream. This began approximately at 2026-02-21 03:10 UTC during the first traffic ramp to canary weight 10%.

Impact:
Multiple enterprise tenants (LotusAI) experienced corrupted or inconsistent responses for ongoing multi-turn sessions. No data leak observed; user-facing application errors and user complaints. Estimated affected sessions ~120 over 25 minutes.

Environment:
- Dedicated deployment for LotusAI (dedicated pool dp-lotus-prod-us-east)
- Routing policy: weighted canary promote with session pin retention policy 'session-lock' enabled
- Canary model: llama-3b-v2-canary (quantized)
- Edge health probing enabled with short probe interval for host liveness

Steps to reproduce:
1) Start a multi-turn session pinned to stable model (llama-3b-v2).
2) Trigger a simulated canary promote with 10% weight to llama-3b-v2-canary.
3) Rapidly flip edge host health (simulate probe failures) on subset of edge proxies during promote window.
4) Continue multi-turn requests; observe model hashes and stream disconnects.

Observed behavior:
- Session that had been pinned to stable model sometimes routed to canary after an edge host health probe caused a rebind at the edge layer.
- Some responses were mixed (prefix tokens from stable model, continuing tokens from canary) leading to incoherent outputs.
- A small number of requests returned 502 mid-stream with logs showing KV cache mismatch/detection in serving-runtime.

Expected behavior:
- Session pins should persist for the duration of the session unless customer explicitly unpins or session TTL expires. Edge health probes should not trigger migration of pinned sessions to canary variant. If host fallback is required, pinned sessions should prefer a compatible pinned variant or fall back to stable variant, not mix models.

Relevant logs/snippets:
- Edge proxy log at 2026-02-21T03:12:06Z: "probe:host_unhealthy host=ep-34 status=503; session_rebind candidate=route-redirect"
- Routing service trace 2026-02-21T03:12:07Z: "session_lock_check: found lock=stable@tenant:12345 ttl=2m but host_rebind=true; applying rebind policy=prefer_any"
- Serving runtime WARN 2026-02-21T03:12:09Z: "kv-cache-consistency: detected model-hash-mismatch incoming=hash-canary existing=hash-stable; terminating stream"
- Application error seen by customer: "Conversation turned nonsense at step 7"
comments: 2026-02-21 03:20 UTC - Liam Chen (Support): Initial report from LotusAI CS. Attached application logs, session IDs, and request IDs. Marked P1 due to enterprise outage.
2026-02-21 03:32 UTC - Sofia Martinez (SRE): Acknowledged. Started capture of routing traces and edge proxy metrics. Reproduced host probe scenario in staging with identical routing config.

2026-02-21 04:05 UTC - Jordan Reyes (Serving Runtime): Observed kv-cache mismatch when session rebinds to an instance serving a different model hash. Hypothesis: edge rebind triggers request to new downstream that doesn't honor session lock semantics across rebind path.

2026-02-21 05:10 UTC - Aisha Patel (Product): Canary promote was configured with 'prefer_any' fallback for host_rebind to reduce blackholing during partial outages. That policy may be in conflict with 'session-lock' semantics. Flagging as policy interaction bug.

2026-02-22 09:15 UTC - Sofia Martinez (SRE): Deployed temporary mitigation: adjusted edge probe aggressiveness for LotusAI pool and set routing fallback to 'prefer_compatible' for affected tenants. Incident symptom rate dropped to near zero.
2026-02-24 11:40 UTC - Liam Chen (Support): Customer confirmed reduced errors and provided sample session IDs that still show intermittent pin drift. Asking for permanent fix ETA.

2026-02-25 14:05 UTC - Sofia Martinez (SRE): Engineering PR prepared to change session-lock precedence during rebind and to carry model-hash in session token. Targeted rollout 2026-03-02 canary for internal clusters.
investigation_notes: Reproduced issue in staging by triggering edge host flaps during a weighted canary promote using the same routing config as production.

Root cause hypothesis: when edge detects host unhealthy and triggers a session rebind, the routing service's rebind policy 'prefer_any' did not consult session lock metadata. Rebind path allowed assignment to an instance running canary model. The serving runtime then detected KV cache model-hash mismatch and terminated stream or produced mixed outputs when partial state was accepted.
Session tokens lacked an embedded model-hash or model-stability flag, so downstream allocator could not enforce 'pin-to-compatible' at rebind time.
Edge probe frequency combined with short session-lock TTL (~2m) made race window measurable during our promote window.
root_cause: Policy interaction: routing fallback policy 'prefer_any' during edge-induced rebinds bypassed session-lock enforcement, allowing pinned sessions to be routed to non-compatible model variants. This caused KV cache mismatches and mixed outputs.
resolution: Mitigation applied: 1) edge probe aggressiveness reduced for affected dedicated pools; 2) temporary routing override 'prefer_compatible' applied for LotusAI tenant; 3) emergency patch to routing service to check session-lock metadata on rebind is merged (PR #918) and staged for internal canary. Full rollout after internal validation.
